title: Turbulent viscosity models: specifying the viscosity, and the flows the hypothesis cannot describe
status: reviewed and locally validated; passes 1-9 complete; gate 6b round 2 had 3 blocking defects, fixed by a reviser and checked by the lead (no round 3)
transcript_provenance: Local machine transcription (faster-whisper small.en); not publisher captions
source_uncertainties: Speech 'the Reynolds stress is 0' in the straight section (L49 ~23:00) against slide f0046 'the Reynolds stress anisotropies are zero': the chapter follows the slide and states that the isotropic part (2/3)k delta_ij remains.
Speech calls the intrinsic assumption 'proportional to the mean strain rate'; slide f0042 says 'determined by'. The chapter follows the slide.

Speech '90 percent of the cost for 10 percent of the energy' is labelled arbitrary by the speaker; slide f0032 says over 99 % of the effort is devoted to the dissipation range. The chapter checks the direction and a threshold, not the figure.
The slide figure f0044 labels the contraction strain as S_11 = (symbol unreadable, written S_k) and S_22 = S_33 = -1/2 of it; the chapter calls it the axial strain without a symbol.
The slide on the Newtonian law (f0043) writes -(tau_ij + P delta_ij)/rho = -2 nu S_ij; the chapter does not reuse its sign convention.
Citations printed on the slides (Kim et al. 1987; Warhaft 1980; Uberoi 1956; Tucker 1970) were not opened and are reported as the slides' citations.

Module source: Lecture 49 shows no Source slide; the attribution of the module to Pope (2000) is the speech of L43 3:00 (as in chapter 17) and the Figure 10.1 caption of the contraction sketch. The book was not available, so no Pope page, equation or value appears in the chapter.

The k-epsilon equations and constants are checked in the OpenFOAM documentation page and on p. 23 of Michael et al. (2023); the original Launder and Spalding (1974) and Jones and Launder (1972) papers were not opened.
